metadata.name: WritingLayouts
metadata.description: Guides > Writing layouts. Task-focused walk-through of how to author layout JSON well — style definitions, include (sub-layout reuse), Collection basics and multi-section patterns, @{binding} and visibility tricks, and common pitfalls. Seven sections + TOC + next-reads. Web (rjui) focused because this docs site is Web-primary; cross-platform nuances deferred to concept essays.

methods.name: onAppear
methods.description: Seed nextReadLinks from the module-scope NEXT_READ_ENTRIES catalog (two rows: next_custom_components -> /guides/custom-components, next_first_spec -> /guides/writing-your-first-spec) and stamp currentLanguage from StringManager.language. Each row's titleKey / descriptionKey is resolved through StringManager with the guides_writing_layouts_ namespace prefix.

methods.name: onNavigate
methods.description: Client-side navigation via router.push(url). Destinations are the spec-mapped URLs enumerated in transitions: /, /guides/custom-components, /guides/writing-your-first-spec.

vars.name: nextReadLinks
vars.description: Two closing 'read next' cards pointing at /guides/custom-components and /guides/writing-your-first-spec. Seeded by onAppear from the NEXT_READ_ENTRIES static catalog.

relatedFiles.description: Layout source of truth (hand-edited, distributed to jsonui-doc-web/src/Layouts/guides/writing-layouts.json by jui build).

notes: Sixth live entry under the Guides tab. Follows the same template as the other five (custom-components, localization, navigation, testing, writing-your-first-spec).

Seven sections: (1) Orient yourself (where layout / cell / style / strings files live, with project tree), (2) Style definitions (styles/ folder, 'style' attribute, merge rule, no inheritance) with 2 CodeBlocks, (3) Include sub-layout reuse ('include' attribute, shared_data + data, not recursive) with 1 CodeBlock, (4) Collection basics — single cell type with items / cellIdProperty / sections / orientation / columnCount / line-itemSpacing / lazy / scrollEnabled; data block on the cell side that becomes a TS Data interface, with 3 CodeBlocks, (5) Collection multi-section — mixing cell types requires multiple sections because rjui cannot pick cell type dynamically per row, with 1 CodeBlock, (6) Binding and visibility — @{property} resolution + visible/invisible/gone triage, (7) Pitfalls — weight vs matchParent in flex-row, topMargin is orientation-agnostic, gone vs invisible DOM implications, _overlay is internal.

Running exemplars: home.json styles ('primary_button', 'hero_section'), cells/agent_row.json for the cell data block example, and a minimal include example even though JsonUIDocument itself does not currently use the include mechanism (it is a supported feature worth documenting).
Cross-links: the five existing guides' next-reads will be touched in a follow-up so at least custom-components points to this guide as a natural follow-on.

2026-09-03 - section_collection_basic_bullet_lazy was wrong: it described `lazy` as a boolean (true / false) while the attribute SSoT declares a string enum 'lazy' | 'eager' | 'none' (or a binding). Measured in a scratch copy: a Collection with lazy:false gets the build warning 'Attribute lazy in Collection expects string or binding, got boolean', and lazy:'none' gets none. Rewritten with the three values and the flow scroll rule (with lazy in effect a flow Collection scrolls inside its own bounds; 'none' only wraps). Found by comparing the site's words with the SSoT sentence the release changed - the declaration itself reaches no runtime file here.

2026-09-03, a published page was printing an identifier. The full-namespace live check (every key of guides_writing_layouts, both languages) reported section_collection_basic_bullet_scrollEnabled absent; the page was rendering the KEY NAME where the bullet belongs. Cause is upstream: rjui's layout-to-TSX conversion does not recognise a string key containing an uppercase letter and emits it as literal text - the sibling bullets became {$s....BulletLazy} lookups while this one became the bare word. jui build exits 0 with zero warnings and every gate was green, so nothing here could have caught it. Of this site's 1988 string keys exactly two carried an uppercase letter and both were broken and published (the other is on the developer-menu page); renaming them to lowercase, with their layout references, restored the lookup. Filed upstream. Two unseeded leftovers, next_custom_components_title and _description, were removed from this namespace at the same time - the reference_components copies are the ones the view model reads.

2026-10-02 — section_include_body rewritten. Include semantics follow the user ruling ( 2026-10-02, 'follow the declaration; keep the maps as overrides'): an include is an inline expansion; the included layout reads the including screen's data, which that screen's ViewModel owns; an `id` on the include prefixes the included layout's data names; the include's `shared_data` then `data` maps are laid over that data. The sentence that said the include 'passes any shared_data / data fields on the include as props' is gone. section_binding_body: 'starts with @{name}' becomes 'is one whole @{name}', and the mixed form is named as warned. jsonui-cli has binding-mixed-text (WARNING, fails under --strict): an SSoT-declared attribute whose value contains `@{` but is not one whole `@{...}`. The user's ruling (2026-10-02) is that a sentence is assembled in the ViewModel and passed as one binding, because a layout-assembled sentence cannot be localized as one string and puts logic in the JSON.

2026-10-02 — section_include_note_depth said include was one level deep, with the included file's includes not followed. That was false: upstream reports that every expander (sjui / kjui / rjui / Python / the SJUI and KJUI runtimes) expands nesting recursively and stops on a cycle with an error. The bullet now states recursion and the nested data rules: prefixes compose (side + card + title → sideCardTitle); an inner map's values bind in the outer partial's scope, after the outer map; an inner include without a map only takes the prefix. Upstream's word, relayed by the orchestrator; not measured here.

2026-11-10: section_include_note_place added under the include section: on web an included layout's root takes its place in the including container (overlay placement, row axis for a matchParent height, distribution, wrapContent cap), via a jsonuiPlace prop and the generated includePlace helper; read from the JSX jui build wrote on a scratch web project (add "absolute bottom-0 left-0" in an overlay, add "self-stretch" / drop "flex-1 min-w-0 min-h-0" in a row, nothing for the same include alone). Rendered positions are jsonui-cli's word. section_pitfalls_bullet_visibility: the 'uniform across platforms' sentence says iOS honours a literal visibility on a relatively placed child; read from the sjui converter's output, drawing is jsonui-cli's measurement.

2026-11-10: section_include_note_place: the container runs applyRelativePositions for an include root constrained against a sibling (scratch web project: emitted for alignTopOfView "anchor"). New section_pitfalls_bullet_relative_overlap: in a View with no orientation and a sibling-constrained child, unconstrained children share the grid's one cell on web (alignBottom child: col-start-1 row-start-1 self-end); drawing is jsonui-cli's measurement; the site has 0 sibling constraints.

2026-11-10: section_include_note_place: constraint targets inside an include with an id get the include's prefix in sjui, kjui and rjui codegen (include expansion of sjui/kjui: sidePin alignTopOfView anchor -> sideAnchor; rjui JSX: above jsonuiIncludeId(idPrefix, "anchor")); per-platform symptoms without the prefix are jsonui-cli's word.

2026-11-11: section_include_note_place: the Dynamic sentence covers SwiftJsonUI / KotlinJsonUI (jsonui-cli's word, runtimes not run). New bullets: section_pitfalls_bullet_gone_anchor (gone has no box; drawn in headless Chromium via jsonui-cli's rjui_chromium_draw harness with own fixtures: gone anchor 0,0, visible control 0,30; isGone read from sjui output), section_pitfalls_bullet_center_margin (centerInParent + leftMargin/topMargin 20: 40,40, equal to the no-margin control; alignLeft control 20,0), section_pitfalls_bullet_build_checks (ERROR [relative-constraints] for parent/cousin/self/missing targets, sibling control not named, web-only exit 1 and 0 with --allow-partial; INFO [ios-tap] for a 20x20 Button with iOS configured, 44x44 not named).

2026-11-12: section_include_note_ids added after section_include_note_place. On web, Segment/TabView `<id>_tab_<n>`, Collection `<id>_item_<n>` and a custom component's id take the include's prefix; read from the TSX jui build wrote on a scratch web project and the generated includeId helper, no page rendered. iOS/Android spelling is jsonui-cli's word. The site has no include, so no id moves.

2026-11-13: section_pitfalls_bullet_weight gained the unequal-weight cross-axis rule, read from SwiftJsonUI's WeightedStackView (fillsCrossAxis only for matchParent; otherwise the largest child); drawing parity is jsonui-cli's conformance measurement, nothing drawn here.

2026-11-13: section_collection_reorder_* added at the end of section 5 (reorderable / onReorder / reorderHandle / reorderLockedProperty). Measured: rjui's CollectionConverter on the example (wraps the rows in JsonuiReorderSection/Item with handleId, locked and a bound enabled); the generated web helper's release/a11y functions run in Node on 5 rows with index 2 locked, header and footer 40 (header -> first allowed place, footer -> last, outside -> cancel, a locked row not picked up, no move past it, no move-up/down button into it), equal to shared/core/reorder_rule.py; reorder_info.tree_lines on variants (stack path named below 27 or unread, not at 27, not with a handle, locked property, listStyle or no sections); LayoutValidator.check_collection (warning for true or a binding without cellIdProperty, not blocking). iOS/Android drawing and VoiceOver/TalkBack are jsonui-cli's word; nothing dragged here.
2026-11-14: section_pitfalls_bullet_selectbox added. iOS / Android padding and Android's 56dp removal are jsonui-cli's word.

2026-11-14: reorder bullets fixed / pass / callbacks / change added after locked; a11y and ios bullets extended; note_measured re-measured (rjui CollectionConverter passes onReorderStart/End and fixed; helper in Node: 60-high rows, dy 31 passes; fixed row 2 passed (row 1 -> 3), locked stops at 1; a11y skips the fixed row and offers moves past it; itemsChanged true on reorder / add / fixed change, false on same ids; reorder_info: callbacks take a stack off the ios-reorder line, a List with callbacks gets INFO [ios-reorder-callbacks]). section_pitfalls_bullet_selectbox web part written from SelectBoxConverter (svg in currentColor beside the select, caretAttributes.tintColor and fontColor colour it, src keeps its own, rightMargin moves it).
